thread:
Priya: Heads-up — we need a quick sync on audit-event visibility across services (api-gw, auth, console, billing, runtime). Found some customer-facing validation failures in staging, want to map gaps and owners.

Alex: +1. Which failures specifically?

Priya: Two things: (1) missing user_id for token exchange events in api-gw, (2) billing export events losing request_id at runtime -> makes customer replay/validation fail.

Mateo: I saw the token-exchange schema mismatch. The schema in the consumer tests expects 'actor.id' but api-gw emits 'user_id'. Easy to fix but need rollout plan.

Jordan: For billing exports the problem is the batching job strips ctx.request_id when aggregating. We can add a batch-level header but might need a migration to backfill older exports.

Sam: Also flag: RBAC changes last week added new admin grant flows — those aren't being emitted from console as structured audit events, only as opaque logs. Customers asked for structured events for compliance.

Priya: Okay clear. Proposed immediate plan: 1) quick schema alignment for api-gw (actor.id vs user_id), 2) ensure request_id is propagated in billing batch, 3) add structured admin_grant event from console, 4) add unit/integration tests + customer-facing validation harness. Thoughts?

Taylor: Sounds good. I can take (1) and the test harness bits. Will make a small compatibility layer to emit both fields for one release.

Alex: I can take (2) — will update batching job to preserve request_id and add a flag to include original request ids array.

Mateo: I'll own (3) — console PR to emit `audit.event_type = admin_grant` with fields: actor, target, reason, before/after perms.

Priya: Great. Add KMS note: when we add structured admin events we may need to avoid including plaintext secrets. Confirming KMS/HSM integration for storing envelope metadata only.

Sam: Agree. We'll redact secrets at the source and only store KMS-wrapped references. Security-bot: "reminder: do not log secrets or raw tokens; follow PII redaction policy" :warning:

Priya: Also we need to add these to the customer validation suite: a small harness that validates event schema + sig verification and replayability. Example snippet for schema I pushed to docs:```json
{
  "event_type": "admin_grant",
  "timestamp": "2025-05-01T15:12:00Z",
  "actor": {"id": "u-123", "email": "eng+alice@example.com"},
  "target": {"id": "proj-99", "type": "project"},
  "change": {"before": "read", "after": "admin"},
  "request_id": "req-abc-123"
}
```

Jordan: Suggest adding `service` and `region` fields to all events for routing/backfill. Also include `schema_version`.

Taylor: I'll add acceptance tests to the harness that simulate replay with missing fields and ensure we fail-fast for regression.

Alex: timeline? I can do the batching change and a rollout canary in staging today, prod next week if green.

Priya: Let's aim for staging patches today, GA next Thu. Owners add PR links in this thread when created.

Mateo: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/console/pull/421 — draft with admin_grant event shape.

Alex: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/billing/pull/88 — preserves request_id across batches.

Taylor: PR for tests/harness: https://git.internal/redwood/security/pull/210 — harness accepts schema bundles and runs validation and sig checks.

Sam: I'll file a runbook note for KMS handling and redaction: https://docs.internal/redwood/security/kms-audit.

security-bot: New issue created: SEC-2025: audit-events-schema-mismatch (priority: high).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for billing-batch (canary=10%).

Priya: Thanks all — after PRs link, I'll compile a short customer note for affected tenants and include rollback instructions. :thumbsup:

Alex: linked prod telemetry dashboards to the thread: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/audit/events - will monitor request_id rates.

Mateo: will follow up with a short migration plan for historical export backfill if needed.

Priya: Perfect. Closing loop later today with status update.
